# tails — full notes for coding agents

Import: `import tails`. PyPI / pip name: `rare-tails` (the name `tails` is
taken on PyPI). Repo: https://github.com/rare-labs/tails
Docs: https://rare-labs.github.io/tails/

## Purpose

Extreme-value analysis in Python, designed to run one series or a large batch
in a single call (JAX `vmap` + a Newton optimiser with exact Hessians).

Use it for return levels, return periods, non-stationary GEV/GPD/POT, and
intensity–duration–frequency curves. If the user has one pandas time series
and wants diagnostic plots first, mention pyextremes. If they already use
xclim, they can keep calling xclim: `import tails.xclim` first, then
`frequency_analysis(..., backend="tails", ci="profile")` from
`xclim.compute.stats` (xclim 1.0 and later) or `xclim.indices.stats`
(xclim 0.x). tails also has covariate models and IDF.

## Install

pip install rare-tails
# extras: xarray, plots, bayes, xclim, dev, docs, all
# Python >= 3.10. CPU by default (jax[cpu]); GPU needs a CUDA build of jax.

## API

tails.fit_gev(data, loc=None, scale=None, shape=None, mask=None, method="mle")
  data: shape (*batch, n). NaN = missing. method: "mle" | "gmle" | "lmom".
  Returns GEVFit.
  fit.params is a dict with natural parameters loc, scale, shape (arrays).
  fit.return_level(periods, ci="profile"|"delta"|"bootstrap", alpha=0.05)
  Profile and bootstrap apply to stationary GEV and to GEV with covariates
  (the profile replaces the location intercept at each covariate row).
  fit.coef, fit.se, fit.summary(), fit.converged, fit.nobs, fit.loglik.

tails.fit_gpd(data, threshold=None, ...)
tails.fit_pot(data, threshold, npy=365.25, ...)
  POT return_level ci is "delta", "profile" or "bootstrap" (stationary).
  Profile is the joint excess + exceedance-rate likelihood. fixed_shape
  stays fixed for delta and profile; bootstrap needs a free shape.

tails.block_maxima, decluster_runs, extremal_index
tails.mean_residual_life, parameter_stability, select_threshold
tails.plot_threshold(x, thresholds=None, *, unit="", alpha=0.05, n_boot=199, seed=0)
  One series (1-d array or pandas Series). Draws the mean-excess ribbon, the
  modified scale σ − ξu and the shape ξ, and a dashed line at the ForwardStop
  threshold. unit is an axis label ("mm", "kN", ...). Requires rare-tails[plots],
  the same ImportError as plot_diagnostics. Returns (fig, axes), three panels.

from tails.records import record_breaks, foster_stuart, record_indicators, record_test
  record_breaks(x, kind="upper"|"lower") -> RecordBreaks
    Last axis is the series. NaN is skipped and does not advance the trial.
    A tie is not a record. The first finite value is a record.
    .summary() one row per series: observed, expected (H_n), variance, ratio, p-values.
    .events(series=0) one row per record: time, value, trial, records_so_far, expected_so_far.
    pvalue is one-sided for more records than the harmonic law.
  foster_stuart(x) -> FosterStuart
    From trial 2 on, D = upper records − lower records (mean 0; positive is an upward drift).
    S = upper + lower (mean sum_{t=2}^n 2/t). pvalue_up, pvalue_trend, pvalue_spread.
  record_indicators(x, kind) and record_test(x, kind) are the same counts.

from tails.idf import IDFData, fit_idf, scaling_test
  data = IDFData.from_eccc("701S001")
  fit_idf(data, "general"|"simple", "matern"|"exponential"|None)
  scaling_test(data, "simple"|"general") -> p-value
  idf.quantile_ci(durations, periods, method="hessian"|"sandwich"|"bootstrap")
  idf.plot(periods=(2,10,25,100), ci="hessian")  # log-log curves, CI ribbons,
                                                 # empirical T-year points in mm/h vs hours
  fit.plot_diagnostics(ci="profile")             # stationary: QQ/PP, RL ribbon, density
                                                 # non-stationary GEV: trend along the covariate
  rl.plot()                                      # ReturnLevels ribbon
  tails.plot_return_level_map(levels, lon, lat, period=100)
    One return level per location. Stations: scatter. A (lat, lon) grid: mesh.
    lon/lat are degrees from the data (or lat/lon, latitude/longitude on an
    xarray DataArray; a Dataset uses its return_level variable). Colour is the
    level in the units of the fit — label= names them, or a DataArray units
    attribute. Default colour bar is "Return level". period= is required when
    more than one period is present (period or return_period). NaNs are omitted.
    ReturnLevels.plot_map(lon, lat, period=100) is the same function.
    Axes are degrees, aspect 1/cos(mean latitude), with no tile layer.

from tails.datasets import load_eccc_quebec, load_idfcurves, parse_eccc_idf, eccc_daily, eccc_hourly
  eccc_daily("701S001", 2020) / eccc_hourly(station, (2019, 2020))
  Official API: https://api.weather.gc.ca (cached under $TAILS_CACHE or ~/.cache/tails).
  load_eccc_quebec() -> DataFrame with station_id, name, lat, lon, elevation,
  year, and duration columns 5min, 10min, 15min, 30min, 1h, 2h, 6h, 12h, 24h.
  151 Québec stations, ECCC IDF v3.40.

import tails.xarray as tx
  tx.fit_gev(da, dim="time"); tx.return_level(ds, [20, 100])
  Coefficients include log_scale. Covariates are supported here.
  tx.fit_idf(intensity, year="year", duration="duration")
    DataArray of annual-maximum intensity (mm/h). depth=True converts mm to mm/h.
    Duration coordinate: hours, a timedelta, or ECCC tags (5min … 24h).
    Chunks must not split year or duration. One batched fit per chunk.
    Dataset of natural parameters (mu0, sigma0, xi, alpha, plus delta / nu / rho),
    <name>_se from the observed Hessian, loglik, converged.
    A cell with fewer than two durations of three finite years is NaN.
  tx.idf_quantile(idf_ds, [1.0], [100])   # intensity at 1 h, 100-year return period
  Worked example: docs/tutorial_quebec_idf.md section 8. Three bundled Québec
  stations as a DataArray of depths (mm), depth=True, marginal="general".
  Québec City 701S001 100-year 1 h intensity is 46.06 mm/h, the same as
  fit_idf(IDFData.from_eccc("701S001"), "general"). Montréal–Trudeau 48.35 mm/h;
  Sherbrooke A (1962–1994) 50.77 mm/h.

import tails.xclim   # before `from xclim... import frequency_analysis`
  from xclim.compute.stats import frequency_analysis, fit   # xclim >= 1.0
  from xclim.indices.stats import frequency_analysis, fit   # xclim 0.x
  frequency_analysis(da, "max", [20, 100], "genextreme", backend="tails", ci="profile")
  fit(da, dist="genextreme", method="ML", backend="tails")  # also "PWM", "GMLE"; dim="time"
  fa(block_maxima, [20, 100], dist="genextreme", backend="tails", ci="delta"|"profile"|"bootstrap")
  fit returns dparams c, loc, scale and scipy_dist, so parametric_quantile still works.
  genextreme c = -ξ. genpareto c = ξ.
  Omit backend (or pass "scipy" / "xclim") to keep xclim's scipy fit.
  ci set returns a Dataset (return_level, lower, upper); ci omitted returns a DataArray.
  Stationary only. mode="min" reflects the sample, fits a GEV, and reflects the level.
  fit() itself fits the given sample. GPD quantiles are quantiles of the fitted
  sample (scalar threshold= adds it back); annual POT levels stay on tails.fit_pot.
  Indexers are xclim's (month, season, ...). frequency_analysis needs a datetime
  coordinate. Short GEV records (<3 finite values) come back as NaN.
  Entry point: xclim.stats.backends → tails.xclim:register. Optional extra: rare-tails[xclim].

from tails.bayes import fit_gev_bayes   # requires rare-tails[bayes]

## Worked example (real bundled data — do not invent other numbers)

Station 701S001, QUEBEC JEAN LESAGE INTL, 64 years (1961–2024), 24-hour
annual maxima. Wettest year: 2005, 105.4 mm.

fit = tails.fit_gev(y)  # y = the 24h column
# GEVFit(loc=51.66±1.6, log_scale=2.453±0.097, shape=-0.02595±0.078, loglik=-256.9124)
# params: loc=51.65798, scale=11.62282, shape=-0.02594891
# return_level([20, 100], ci="profile"):
#   estimate [84.883, 102.057]
#   lower    [77.811,  90.504]
#   upper    [97.962, 131.119]
# Return period of 105.4 mm: 138.3 years.
# tails.how_rare(depth, "2005-01-01", ci="profile", unit="mm", name="Québec City")
#   "A value of 105.4 mm in 2005 at Québec City is a 1-in-138-year event (95% CI: 30–1212 years)."
# Public how_rare examples in docs/howto.md (annual maxima; sources in that page):
#   Treasury 10-year, 39 basis points in 1994: "A value of 39 basis points in 1994 is a 1-in-74-year event (95% CI: 13–758 years)."
#   Henry Hub, 23.86 USD per million Btu in 2021: "A value of 23.86 USD per million Btu in 2021 is a 1-in-24-year event (95% CI: 7.1–70 years)."
#   US initial claims, 6.137 million in 2020: "A value of 6.137 million claims in 2020 is a 1-in-6654-year event (95% CI: 4251–50099 years)."
#   USGS Mw 9.5 in 1960: "A value of 9.5 Mw in 1960 is a 1-in-123-year event (95% CI: 29–1004 years)."
# record_breaks on the same 64 annual maxima: 7 upper records, expected 4.74
# (ratio 1.48, one-sided p=0.16). Years: 1961, 1962, 1978, 1979, 1996, 1998, 2005
# (61.7, 71.4, 78.9, 81.2, 83.0, 104.8, 105.4 mm).
# foster_stuart: D=2 (pvalue_up=0.29), S=10 against 7.49 expected.

1-hour annual maximum 59.9 mm in 1979: single-duration GEV return period
129.1 years. 20- and 100-year 1-hour levels 39.67 and 56.75 mm (profile CIs
wide: 100-year 44.2–99.5 mm).

Québec IDF tutorial notebook: docs/notebooks/tutorial_quebec_idf.ipynb
Open in Colab: https://colab.research.google.com/github/rare-labs/tails/blob/main/docs/notebooks/tutorial_quebec_idf.ipynb

IDF on the same station, general scaling + Matérn Gaussian copula:
params (mu0, sigma0, xi, alpha, delta, nu, rho) ≈
(19.886, 5.706, -0.04467, 0.7143, 0.04461, 0.9168, 2.431)
100-year 1-hour intensity 43.61 mm/h, Wald 95% CI [39.46, 47.77].
scaling_test simple ≈ 0.00787 (reject); general ≈ 0.778 (compatible).

Batch: all 151 bundled stations, 24-hour maxima padded with NaN, all 151
GEV fits converged. Québec City's 100-year level in the batch equals the
single-station fit (102.0568 mm). Cap Tourmente 7041177 has nobs=11 and
ξ≈1.24; do not quote its 100-year level.

## Pitfalls

- scipy.stats.genextreme shape c equals minus tails/Coles ξ.
- First JAX call compiles (seconds); later calls are fast. Compiled kernels are cached on disk
  ($TAILS_CACHE/jax, default ~/.cache/tails/jax), so new sessions start warm. TAILS_JAX_CACHE=0 turns it off.
- Last axis is the record; preceding axes are the batch.
- Plot APIs: fit.plot_diagnostics() on a stationary GEV/GPD/POT, or a non-stationary GEV trend (observations, fitted return level along the covariate, ribbon); tails.plot_threshold(series, unit=...) for threshold choice; ReturnLevels.plot(); IDFFit.plot(); tails.plot_return_level_map(levels, lon, lat) / ReturnLevels.plot_map. No GEVFit.plot(). All need rare-tails[plots]. The map takes longitude and latitude from the data; the colour is the return level in the units of the fit.
- Do not put IDFCurves.jl author names in new public text; see NOTICE.
- Do not add a public planning document or a benchmark suite to this repository.
